paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples.

model_annotations.English: The plot illustrates the performance of two methods—ST-ES (blue line with circular markers) and Random (orange line with circular markers)—in terms of minADE₂₀, which is shown on the y-axis with a linear scale ranging from 8.80 to 10.20, as the number of in-context examples increases along the x-axis, which is also on a linear scale from 0 to 8 with tick marks at integer intervals. The ST-ES method starts at a minADE₂₀ of approximately 10.20 when zero examples are provided, then drops sharply to about 9.20 at 1 example, continues decreasing gradually to around 8.88 at 6 examples, and stabilizes near 8.88 by 8 examples. In contrast, the Random method begins at approximately 9.78 with zero examples, dips to about 9.48 at 2 examples, remains relatively flat around 9.48 to 9.52 from 2 to 6 examples, and then rises slightly to about 9.60 at 8 examples. Throughout the range of example numbers, the ST-ES method consistently achieves lower minADE₂₀ values than the Random method.
model_annotations.German: The plot illustrates the performance of two methods—ST-ES (blue line with circular markers) and Random (orange line with circular markers)—in terms of minADE₂₀ (a metric for trajectory prediction accuracy) as the number of in-context examples varies from 0 to 8. The x-axis, labeled “Number of Examples,” is linearly scaled from 0 to 8 with tick marks at integer intervals. The y-axis, labeled “minADE₂₀ (←)”, is also linearly scaled, ranging from 8.80 to 10.20 with tick marks at 0.20 intervals. For the ST-ES method, the minADE₂₀ starts at 10.20 when no examples are provided, drops sharply to 9.20 at 1 example, and then gradually decreases to approximately 8.88 at 8 examples, showing a consistent improvement with more examples. In contrast, the Random method begins at 9.80 with 0 examples, decreases slightly to around 9.40 at 2 examples, and then remains relatively stable between 9.40 and 9.60 across the remaining number of examples, indicating minimal improvement beyond 2 examples.
